title: Allot Leads Founding Industry and Academic Consortium to Launch Israeli Post-Quantum Communications Initiative - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Allot Ltd. has been named founding member and Chair of a new Israeli national consortium developing post-quantum communications protocols across optical, satellite and mobile networks, backed by the Israel Innovation Authority and joining NVIDIA, Elta Systems, and six universities.

insights.claim: Allot Ltd. (NASDAQ: ALLT) has been appointed founding member and Chair of Israel's newly established Post-Quantum Communications (PQC) Consortium, which is supported by the Israel Innovation Authority's Technological Infrastructure Division.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Allot secures a leadership position in national PQC infrastructure standard-setting, giving it early visibility and credibility in a fast-forming regulatory-driven market segment.
insights.locator: Cybersecurity and network intelligence vendor Allot Ltd.

insights.claim: Allot VP and CTO Dr. Yaakov Stein chairs both the Consortium Board and its Scientific Committee, coordinating R&D between corporate partners and Israeli university research labs.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Identifies the key technical gatekeeper likely to influence future consortium-driven standards or procurement decisions.
insights.locator: Consortium Governance: Allot VP CTO Dr. Yaakov Stein

insights.claim: The consortium brings together corporate partners NVIDIA, Elta Systems, RAD Data Communications, Ceragon, Classiq, Gilat Satellite Networks, Heqa, and Ribbon Communications alongside six Israeli universities (Technion, Bar-Ilan, Hebrew University, Ben-Gurion, Open University, and University of Haifa) to build quantum-safe protocols for optical, satellite, and mobile networks.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Signals which vendors are positioning early for PQC infrastructure contracts in Israel; watch Ceragon, Gilat, Allot, and Classiq for downstream commercial protocol wins.

insights.claim: The consortium's research focuses on defending against 'harvest now, decrypt later' (HNDL) attacks and future cryptanalytically relevant quantum computers (CRQCs) by evaluating pure PQC software algorithms, physical-layer quantum key distribution (QKD), and hybrid PQC-QKD architectures.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Frames the near-term commercial thesis: telecoms and enterprises must migrate encryption now against data-harvesting risk, well before a cryptanalytically relevant quantum computer exists.

insights.claim: The Israeli PQC initiative is explicitly aligned with global government mandates requiring critical infrastructure operators and telecom providers to migrate toward NIST-standardized post-quantum algorithms and hybrid quantum-safe architectures.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Regulatory mandates create a forced-adoption timeline, a structural revenue driver for PQC and hybrid PQC-QKD vendors participating in the consortium.
insights.locator: The initiative aligns with global government mandates
